facts.text: No published method or standard was found that sets a required number of virtual job sites for an ISO 21815-type off-road validation programme.
facts.quote: No off-road standard prescribing a required number of virtual job sites for an ISO 21815-type validation programme was found

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 states requirements and scope rather than requiring validation in a specified number of mines and construction sites.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-3 states requirements and scope, not "validate in N mines and N construction sites"

facts.text: Teams argue the sufficiency of virtual job-site validation through coverage of a defined operating domain and its parameters, rather than counts of sites.
facts.quote: Teams argue sufficiency through coverage of a defined operating domain and its parameters, not through counts of sites.

facts.text: A numerical virtual-site target alone is weak: two hundred nearly identical dry open-pit roads provide less safety coverage than a much smaller set spanning different geometry, materials, object states and environmental extremes.
facts.quote: two hundred nearly identical dry open-pit roads give less safety coverage than a much smaller set that deliberately spans different geometry, materials, object states and environmental extremes.

facts.text: NIST's combinatorial-testing programme constructs smaller test suites covering interactions among parameters rather than enumerating the full Cartesian product.

facts.text: NIST's combinatorial-testing evidence concerns general software and systems testing and does not prove that pairwise testing or any particular t-way strength is sufficient for collision avoidance.

facts.text: An expert-opinion test-space decomposition for off-road virtual job-site validation covers site structure, machine geometry, sensor configuration, operating manoeuvre, object class and size, relative trajectory, speed, visibility and occlusion, weather and light, surface and material, ground traction and deformation, sensor fault and contamination, and braking-system state. This decomposition is consistent with scenario and combinatorial practice but is not an ISO requirement.
